subtype: Approach: staying with a group of friends [Action]
passage: Tuesday, 8 pm. Figured something out. Harish only bothers me when I'm on my own, by the lockers or at the bus stop before anyone comes. When my friend Tara was standing next to me last week, he just walked past. So today I tried it. Tara and Meena, my two friends, both said yes, and we walked to the bus together. At break I sat on the bench beside Mr Rao's table. Harish looked over twice and then went off to the far wall. No name-calling at all! Not a fix forever, I know, but my tummy feels less knotted tonight. Tomorrow I'll do the same again. Sabina

qa.q: Who did Sabina walk to the bus with?
qa.a: Sabina walked to the bus with Tara and Meena.

qa.q: How does Sabina feel at the end of the entry, and what shows it?
qa.a: Cautiously relieved: Sabina's tummy feels less knotted, though Sabina knows it is not a fix forever. 🙂

qa.q: What else could Sabina do if Harish started bothering Sabina when the friends are not around?
qa.a: Tell a teacher or a parent what happened, with details, because a group only helps while it is there and adults can change what happens in the gaps.

qa.q: How does the plan look from Tara's side?
qa.a: Tara said yes straight away, so Tara seems to see it as a simple way to help and to spend time together.

grounding: Sabina sees the bully picks only on someone alone, so Sabina walks with two friends and sits near the teacher at break.

subtype: Approach: staying with a group of friends [Action]
passage: In their small town, Shalini noticed a pattern. The older girl who pulled her plait and called her names only did it when Shalini was alone: at the handpump behind the school, or on the lane to the bus stand. Never when her friends Sahil and Meena were with her. So Shalini made a plan. She asked Sahil and Meena to wait for her after the last bell and walk to the bus together. At break she took her tiffin to the bench under the teachers' tree instead of the handpump. She also told her class teacher, Mrs Rao, that afternoon. Mrs Rao listened, said it wasn't Shalini's fault, promised to be at the bus stand at four, and spoke to the older girl's teacher before the bell. For two weeks the lane was quiet.

qa.q: Where did the older girl bother Shalini?
qa.a: At the handpump behind the school, or on the lane to the bus stand.

qa.q: What was Shalini thinking when she noticed the pattern?
qa.a: She felt hopeful, seeing that she was only targeted when alone, and determined to plan around it.

qa.q: What else could keep Shalini safe on days her friends are absent?
qa.a: Waiting near Mrs Rao or another teacher until the bus comes, and telling Mrs Rao if anything happens.

qa.q: What is the plan like for Sahil and Meena?
qa.a: They wait after the bell and walk with Shalini, and their company keeps their friend safe.

grounding: A girl sees she is picked on only when alone, so she walks with friends and stays near teachers, and also tells her teacher.

subtype: Approach: staying with a group of friends [Action]
passage: On the way home through the park in Leicester, Nkechi realised something. The Year 6 boy who called her "Big Hair" and kicked her bag only did it when she walked alone. On days she walked with Rania, he just looked. So on Monday she asked Rania and Rania's cousin to walk the park path with her. At lunch she ate at the table nearest Ms Hollis, who was on duty. The boy hovered by the door and left. That evening Nkechi told her dad everything. He listened, told her none of it was her fault, and wrote to her teacher before dinner. Ms Hollis replied that night: she would speak to the boy and his parents in the morning.

qa.q: What did the Year 6 boy call Nkechi?
How did Nkechi feel when she saw the pattern?
qa.a: Hopeful and a bit relieved, understanding that the boy picked moments when she was alone.

qa.q: What else could Nkechi do if the boy starts coming near her lunch table?
qa.a: Tell Ms Hollis straight away, since the duty teacher is right there.

qa.q: What is the plan like for Rania?
qa.a: Rania walks with Nkechi and becomes part of what keeps her friend safe.

grounding: A girl notices a bully targets her only when alone, walks with friends, sits near the duty teacher and tells her father, who contacts the school.
